title: Sets, Intersections & Venn Diagrams
coreInsight: Sets represent membership in conditions, and intersections make simultaneous membership and overlap explicit.
targetLearnerRealization: Set regions represent membership in conditions; intersection means satisfying both and mathematical union includes the overlap.
learningObjectives: Place objects into the four regions determined by two set conditions.
Distinguish intersection from inclusive union and include the overlap in mathematical or.
Read set, union, intersection, and outside counts from a Venn diagram.

continuity.openingCallback: C1 allowed direct addition only across cases that did not overlap; now one object will satisfy two conditions at once.
closingSeeds: Adding two set totals counts their shared intersection twice, so one copy must be removed.

misconceptionTargets.misconception: Everything belongs to at least one displayed set.
The region outside both sets can be ignored when it is part of the universe.

beats.purpose: Reactivate C1's disjoint-case check while making simultaneous membership and the outside region unavoidable.
beats.expectedRealization: Two yes-or-no properties create four distinct membership regions, including both and neither.
beats.transitionIn: C1 said we may add separate cases only after checking that they overlap nowhere. This time, some cards deliberately satisfy two descriptions.
beats.transitionOut: The middle is not a bookkeeping mistake: it is the home of every card satisfying both conditions.
beats.prompt: Sort each card by the conditions it satisfies: red, triangle, both, or neither.

visual.ariaLabel: Empty two-set board for red cards and triangle cards, with an outside region

response.feedback: Test each property separately; a card may pass zero, one, or both tests.

beats.correctFeedback: Exactly—each card has one home determined by its two membership answers.
beats.incorrectFeedback: Ask two independent questions about each card: Is it red? Is it a triangle? Use the pair of answers.

visual.ariaLabel: Four cards correctly placed by red and triangle membership

steps.title: Run both tests
steps.body: The red triangle answers yes to both conditions, while the blue square answers no to both.

steps.title: Check coverage and non-overlap
steps.body: Every card gives exactly one of the four answer pairs: yes-no, yes-yes, no-yes, or no-no. So every card is placed once.

resolution.takeaway: Two conditions split the whole universe into four complete, non-overlapping regions.

beats.purpose: Let the learner discover inclusive mathematical or from the completed concrete sort before formal vocabulary appears.
beats.expectedRealization: Red or triangle includes the shared red-triangle region as well as both exclusive regions.
beats.transitionIn: Keep the same four homes. Now a machine accepts any card that is red or is a triangle.
beats.transitionOut: The accepted collection uses three regions; only the card outside both conditions is rejected.
beats.prompt: Which regions feed the machine? Select every region that contains an accepted card.

visual.ariaLabel: The same red and triangle Venn board with one card in each region

response.feedback: A card passes if at least one condition is true.

beats.correctFeedback: Yes—the middle passes both tests, so it certainly passes at least one.
beats.incorrectFeedback: Check the middle card directly: is the red triangle red or a triangle? It is actually both.

steps.title: Test the three inside regions
steps.body: Red-only cards pass the red test, triangle-only cards pass the triangle test, and middle cards pass both tests.

steps.title: Exclude exactly the opposite
steps.body: Only the neither region fails both conditions.

resolution.takeaway: In mathematics, A or B means at least one of the two—including both.

beats.purpose: Attach set, intersection, and union language only after the learner has constructed and interpreted the regions.
beats.expectedRealization: Intersection names the both region, while union names all three regions inside at least one set.
beats.transitionIn: You have already built the objects. Now give the board its mathematical names.
beats.transitionOut: The notation is a compact way to specify which visible regions belong in a count.
beats.name: Sets, intersection, and union
beats.conciseDefinition: A set collects objects satisfying a condition. A ∩ B is the intersection—objects in both. A ∪ B is the union—objects in A or B or both.
beats.formalization: x ∈ A means x belongs to A; A ∩ B means both conditions; A ∪ B means at least one condition.
beats.memoryHook: Intersection is the shared middle; union unites every region inside either circle.

beats.purpose: Translate the concrete four-region sort into a numerical union count without invoking inclusion-exclusion.
beats.expectedRealization: A union is counted once by adding its three disjoint Venn regions.
beats.transitionIn: Replace each card by a region count. Because the regions themselves do not overlap, C1's addition rule works again.
beats.transitionOut: The three inside regions form the union; the outside count belongs to the universe but not to this union.
beats.whyNow: Small explicit region counts make inclusive union numerical while preserving the board built in the discovery activity.
beats.entryBridge: Count the red-only, both, and triangle-only regions exactly once each.
beats.exitBridge: Three plus two plus four gives nine badges in the union; the one outside badge is not silently discarded.
beats.reusedRepresentation: The same two-condition Venn board, now holding counts instead of individual cards.
learnerPrompts: Which three disjoint regions make up red or triangular?
Why is the middle included exactly once?
beats.correctFeedback: Correct—9 badges are red or triangular.
beats.incorrectFeedback: Add the three regions inside at least one circle. Do not include neither, and do not omit the middle.

visual.ariaLabel: Badge Venn diagram with counts 3, 2, 4, and 1 across the four regions

steps.title: Identify the union
steps.body: Red or triangular covers red only, both, and triangular only.

steps.title: Add disjoint regions
steps.body: Those three regions share no badge, so add them once each.

resolution.takeaway: A union is the three inside regions, with the intersection included once.

beats.purpose: Make the outside region operational and distinguish the universe from the union.
beats.expectedRealization: The universe contains all four regions, while the union omits only neither.
beats.transitionIn: Nine counted the union. The board itself promised ten badges, so one region still matters.
beats.transitionOut: A Venn diagram has a boundary as well as circles: outside both is still inside the stated universe.
beats.prompt: How many badges are in the entire universe shown by the board?

visual.ariaLabel: The badge Venn board including the one badge outside both circles

response.feedback: The whole board contains all four non-overlapping regions.

beats.correctFeedback: Right—the outside badge is not in either set, but it is still in the universe.
beats.incorrectFeedback: The question asks for the whole board, so include the neither region along with the union.

steps.title: Count all four regions
steps.body: The universe is partitioned into red only, both, triangular only, and neither.

steps.title: Compare
steps.body: The union has 9; its exact opposite inside this universe has 1.

resolution.takeaway: Outside both can be ignored only when the question's universe excludes it.

beats.purpose: Use the approved authentic problem to infer unknown region sizes from equal set totals, a known union, and a known intersection.
beats.expectedRealization: Equal set sizes force equal exclusive regions; splitting the non-overlap and restoring the intersection gives each set size.
beats.transitionIn: Now the four-region board hides two of its counts. Equality between the circles supplies the missing structure.
beats.transitionOut: The region method gives 1504 and reveals why subtracting the overlap from the union gives both outer slivers, not one set.
beats.whyNow: Equal-size sets turn membership regions into inferable quantities immediately after the learner can read union and intersection from a Venn board.
beats.entryBridge: Keep the overlap fixed at 1001, then decide what the remaining 1006 union elements represent.
beats.exitBridge: Each outer sliver has 503 elements, so one set contains 503 + 1001 = 1504 elements.
beats.reusedRepresentation: The same two-circle board with the overlap fixed first and the exclusive regions solved next.
learnerPrompts: Which region belongs to both sets, and what does x represent?
Why is 2007 − 1001 the two outer slivers combined rather than one whole set?
When x + x counts the overlap twice, what correction leaves the union?
What value of x makes the corrected count equal 2007?
How do the three disjoint region counts check the union and one set?
beats.incorrectFeedback: Keep your attempt, then split the union into left only, both, and right only. Equal set sizes make the two outer regions equal.

steps.title: Remove the shared middle from the union
steps.body: What remains is both exclusive regions together.

steps.title: Use equal set sizes
steps.body: The sets share the same middle, so equal total sizes force equal outer slivers.

steps.title: Rebuild one set
steps.body: Set A contains its exclusive sliver and the entire intersection.

resolution.takeaway: A set consists of its exclusive region plus the intersection; the union consists of three disjoint regions.

beats.purpose: Check independently that a set includes its exclusive region and the intersection, but not the other set's exclusive region.
beats.transitionIn: The contest problem hid the outer counts. First practice the simpler reading task with all four regions visible.
beats.transitionOut: A circle total uses exactly two regions: that circle's exclusive part and the shared middle.
beats.whyNow: A direct set-size read isolates the distinction between one set and the full union after the guided problem.
beats.entryBridge: Trace only the regions inside circle A.
beats.exitBridge: Seven A-only markers plus four shared markers give eleven in A.
learnerPrompts: Which two regions lie inside A?
Which displayed counts do not belong to A?
beats.incorrectFeedback: Include A-only and both. Exclude B-only and neither.

visual.ariaLabel: Marker Venn diagram with 7 in A only, 4 in both, 6 in B only, and 1 in neither

steps.body: A includes A only and both.

resolution.takeaway: A circle total includes its share of the middle.

beats.purpose: Transfer membership decisions to number properties and require explicit accounting for neither.
beats.expectedRealization: Among 1 through 12, 1, 5, 7, and 11 are neither even nor multiples of 3.
beats.transitionIn: Membership need not describe colors or clubs. Let arithmetic properties decide the four regions.
beats.transitionOut: Testing both conditions places every integer once, including four outside both circles.
beats.whyNow: Number properties require fresh membership reasoning rather than merely reading supplied Venn counts.
beats.entryBridge: For each integer, test evenness and divisibility by 3 separately.
beats.exitBridge: The complete partition is four even-only, two both, two multiple-of-3-only, and four neither.
learnerPrompts: Which numbers pass neither divisibility test?
Do your four region counts add back to all 12 integers?
beats.correctFeedback: Correct—4 integers are in neither set.
beats.incorrectFeedback: List 1 through 12 and test each number for both properties; do not stop after finding the union.

visual.ariaLabel: Integers 1 through 12 partitioned by evenness and divisibility by 3

steps.title: Test both properties
steps.body: The numbers 1, 5, 7, and 11 are odd and are not multiples of 3.

steps.title: Check completeness
steps.body: The four region sizes account for the whole universe.

resolution.takeaway: A complete Venn partition includes objects satisfying neither condition.

beats.purpose: Require a fresh inclusive-union count in a larger arithmetic universe without giving region counts in advance.
beats.expectedRealization: The multiples of 4 or 6 from 1 through 20 form a seven-element union with 12 counted once.
beats.transitionIn: Finish with an 'or' question whose overlap must be found rather than shown.
beats.transitionOut: Listing the union once gives seven values; listing both sets separately would repeat 12.
beats.whyNow: The learner must construct the union and handle a shared multiple without a prefilled Venn diagram.
beats.entryBridge: Build both lists, then place any shared value in the middle rather than in two final count piles.
beats.exitBridge: The union is 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 18, 20, so it contains seven integers.
learnerPrompts: Which value is in both lists?
How will you count that shared value only once in the union?
beats.incorrectFeedback: List the multiples of 4 and of 6 through 20. Merge the lists so the shared value 12 appears once.

visual.ariaLabel: Multiples of 4 or 6 through 20 with 12 in the intersection

steps.title: Build the two sets
steps.body: Multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20; multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18.

steps.title: Merge inclusively
steps.body: The shared 12 belongs in the union but appears there only once.

resolution.takeaway: Inclusive or keeps the intersection and counts each member once.

beats.purpose: Consolidate the four-region model and all key distinctions before opening the double-counting question.
beats.expectedRealization: Intersection, union, one-set totals, and the universe correspond to precise combinations of the four regions.
beats.transitionIn: Across shapes, counts, and integers, the circles changed labels but the four-region logic stayed fixed.
beats.prompt: Which statements are always true for two sets A and B drawn inside a stated universe? Select all four.

options.text: A ∩ B is the region belonging to both A and B.
A ∪ B contains A only, both, and B only.
Set A contains A only together with the intersection.
The universe includes the neither region as well as the union.
A ∪ B excludes anything that belongs to both sets.

response.feedback: Match each name to visible regions; mathematical or is inclusive.

beats.correctFeedback: Yes—those four statements completely describe how to read the board.
beats.incorrectFeedback: Remember that union includes the middle, and the stated universe extends beyond the circles.

visual.ariaLabel: General two-set Venn diagram labeling all four regions

steps.title: Inside both
steps.body: The intersection is the shared middle.

steps.title: Inside at least one
steps.body: The union is all three regions inside the circles.

steps.title: Inside the universe
steps.body: Add the neither region when counting every object under discussion.

resolution.takeaway: Ask which membership conditions define the target, then combine exactly those non-overlapping regions.

beats.purpose: Create C9's correction problem only after C8's region meanings have been consolidated.
beats.expectedRealization: Adding two set totals colors the intersection twice even though the union needs one copy.
beats.transitionIn: You can now count safely from disjoint regions. But published problems often give circle totals instead of region totals.
beats.prompt: If you add |A| and |B|, which region receives two layers of color—and what single correction would make every member of A ∪ B have one layer?
beats.takeaway: The intersection is duplicated when whole set totals are added. Next, inclusion–exclusion will remove exactly that extra copy.

notes: Draft connector lesson authored with the repo-local mathinking-lesson Skill.
The opening sort keeps all assignments hidden until the learner submits; the completed Venn organization appears only in its resolution.
The approved 2007 AMC 8 Problem 13 is the sole integrated bank problem and uses its controlled five-step animation only after the learner answers.
